sec07-card-sec07-R24.front: Which two vehicle categories may enter diamond-marked HOV lanes at designated openings?
sec07-card-sec07-R24.expected_back: HOV lanes double riders or decal clean cars behind diamond gates.

sec07-card-sec07-R25.front: Contrast your immediate response to red reflectors on lane lines versus red reflectors on an entrance-ramp edge?
sec07-card-sec07-R25.memory_hook: Lane reds correct, edge reds pull-over
sec07-card-sec07-R25.expected_back: Red lane-line reflectors demand instant correction and red edge reflectors demand pullovers.

sec07-card-sec07-R26.front: Pair landing-lane rules for right and left turns with the locations that outlaw three-point turns?
sec07-card-sec07-R26.memory_hook: Rights land right, three-points skip curves
sec07-card-sec07-R26.expected_back: Turns finish rights right and lefts anywhere lawful, and three-point turns dodge curves, hills, and highways.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: Why must you never jerk the wheel into oncoming traffic or off the shoulder to dodge an animal in Florida?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: Never swerve into traffic or off the road for an animal, since the evasion crash beats the animal strike.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: Which daily light windows, roadside terrains, visual cues, and autumn months demand peak animal watchfulness in Florida?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: Animal odds fall with dawn-and-dusk care, heed of crossing signs, woods, and water, roadside scans for eye shine, and October-through-December deer watch.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: How should you warn other drivers, use your brakes and horn, and check mirrors when an animal stands near your lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: Near animals slow down, flash others, ease off with taps and horn, mind freezing deer, and brake hard when the rear is clear.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: How should you steer during an unavoidable animal impact, and who must you contact after hitting a large animal?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: Unavoidable strikes hold the lane under control, and large-animal crashes go to law enforcement.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: How does Florida pair its ban on swerving for wildlife with your duty after striking a large animal?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: Swerve bans beat strike fears, and large-animal hits still report to officers.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: Which four timing, sign, sight, and seasonal factors tell you where wildlife strikes spike?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: Dawn and dusk, signed woods and waters, eye shine, and October deer season focus watch.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: How do headlight flashes affect other drivers versus deer, and what condition allows hard braking?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: Flashes warn drivers but freeze deer, and hard braking needs a clear rear.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: Which headlight setting, glass tools, and pavement guides should you use in thick Florida smoke, fog, or heavy rain?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: Smoke, fog, and downpours demand real headlights on low beams, lights with wipers, defrosted glass, and painted-line guides.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: Beyond turning on low beams, what cabin, traffic-scanning, and vehicle-prep habits keep you safe in low visibility?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: Murky driving also kills cabin distractions, watches for crawling and parked rigs, and keeps glass and lamps clean.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: What lighting law fires whenever your wipers run in rain, and why do the first minutes of a shower stretch stopping distance?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: Wipers summon headlights, fresh rains slick oiled pavement into longer stops, and gaps grow accordingly.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: What happens to your tires during hydroplaning, and which three tire or speed factors trigger it sooner?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: Hydroplaning floats tires off the road into skids, worsened by soft pressure, bald tread, and speed.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: How do soaked brakes misbehave until dried, and what rule governs driving into a flooded Florida roadway?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: Soaked brakes pull or fade until gently dried, and flooded roads always turn back since depth and current hide.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: Why are parking lamps illegal as a substitute in fog or smoke, and what combination must you run instead?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: Fog and smoke take real low-beam headlights with wipers and painted guides, never parking lamps.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: Which three focus, scanning, and maintenance habits pair up during murky weather?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: Murky miles mute cabins, eye slow rigs, and polish glass and lamps.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: How do Florida's wiper-headlight rule, oily early showers, and following-distance adjustments connect?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: Wipers light lamps, fresh rain slicks oil long, and gaps grow with stopping distance.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.front: Which three tire-condition and speed mistakes make floating tires skid hardest on wet pavement?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.expected_back: Floating tires skid worst on soft pressure, bald tread, and speed.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.front: How do you recover brakes splashed through a shallow puddle versus handling a flooded street ahead?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.expected_back: Wet brakes dry under gentle pedals while flooded roads always turn around.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: How many feet ahead do high beams illuminate, above what speed do they help on open roads, and how does glare affect night vision?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: High beams reveal four hundred fifty feet and suit speeds past twenty-five miles per hour, while oncoming glare shrinks night sight.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: When must headlights run at night, at what exact distances must high beams dim, and what rules cover parking lights?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: Night law lights sunset to sunrise, dims within five hundred feet of oncoming and three hundred ahead, bans parking-lights-only driving, and parks lit outside towns.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: How do you avoid overdriving headlights, protect night vision from bright glare, and pass an oncoming vehicle showing just one headlight?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: Night craft avoids overdriving lamps, rests eyes off bright zones, skims lane lines past staring, and hugs right for one-eyed traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.front: Compare the required dimming distance for approaching versus followed traffic, and can you drive dusk-to-dawn on parking lamps?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.expected_back: High beams dim at five hundred feet coming and three hundred going, and dusk-to-dawn lamps never park-only.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.front: Which four visual and lane-positioning habits protect you from dark stops, bright glare, and one-headlight traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.expected_back: Night craft paces light reach, skims lines past stares, rests bright-dazzled eyes, and hugs right for one-eyed comers.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: Which three actions establish Florida residency for driver licensing purposes?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: Florida residency means domiciling here over six straight months, registering to vote, or filing domicile or homestead papers.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: How does Florida licensing distinguish between immigrants, non-immigrants, and United States citizens?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: Immigrants are lawful permanent residents admitted by visa or USCIS adjustment, non-immigrants enter only briefly for a stated purpose, and citizens were born here or naturalized.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: How soon must working or schooling newcomers get a Florida license, and which four groups are excused?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: Residents must carry a Florida license on public roads, working or schooling newcomers within thirty days, while licensed visitors sixteen and up, federal crews, service families, and commuters are excused.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: Which three student, worker, and equipment-operator groups are also exempt from needing a Florida license?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: College students, home-licensed migrant workers, and brief tractor or road-machine operators are also exempt.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: How do the triggers for general Florida residency differ from the specific thirty-day license deadline?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.memory_hook: Filings mark residency, work starts clock
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: Residency turns on domicile, voting, or filings, while the thirty-day clock binds working or schooling newcomers only.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: What core distinction separates permanent immigrants from non-immigrants and citizens?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: Immigrants hold permanent residence, non-immigrants visit briefly for a purpose, and citizens were born or naturalized here.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: How does driving in Florida on an out-of-state license compare with using an International Driving Permit?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: A home-state license alone excuses a visitor sixteen or up, but an international permit works only beside the home-country license.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: How do Florida Class E exam waivers treat reciprocal countries, Germany, vision screening, and Canadians who keep their old card?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: Valid licenses from listed states, Canada, France, Taiwan, and Korea waive both Class E exams, German ones waive skills, vision still applies, and kept Canadian cards force testing.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: What vehicle weight ceiling defines a Florida Class E license, and when does a two-wheeler require an endorsement?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: Class E covers non-commercial vehicles under twenty-six thousand one pounds; motorcycles over fifty cubic centimeters need an endorsement.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: Which three weight, passenger, or cargo thresholds require upgrading to a commercial driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: Commercial licenses govern twenty-six thousand one-plus-pound rigs, sixteen-plus-passenger carriers, and placarded hazmat with vetting.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: How do full Class E exam waivers contrast with the special rules for German licenses and retained Canadian licenses?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.memory_hook: Germany keeps knowledge, kept Canadian tests
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: Most listed foreign and domestic licenses waive both Class E exams, German ones waive skills only, and kept Canadian cards force everything.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: Where is the exact dividing line between a non-commercial Class E license and commercial licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: Class E stops below twenty-six thousand one pounds while commercial duty starts there, at sixteen passengers, or with placarded cargo.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: Which four document categories make up a Florida license application packet, and how must name changes be connected?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: Applicants show primary identification, Social Security or secondary proof, and two address documents, all original, with a marriage, divorce, or court paper bridging name changes.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: Which official documents qualify as primary identification for a United States citizen?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: Citizens identify by government birth certificate, passport or card, consular report, or naturalization or citizenship certificate.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: What primary identification records do lawful immigrants present, and how are Canadians and non-immigrants handled?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: Immigrants show green cards, passport stamps, or asylum or refugee grants; Canadians and non-immigrants show parallel papers.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: Which supplemental forms must international students and exchange visitors bring, and what accompanies travel, parole, or judge orders?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: Students add I-twenty forms, exchange visitors DS-two thousand nineteen forms, refugees extra papers, and travel, parole, and judge-order papers each ride with a passport.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: What interim credential can a non-citizen receive while federal and state agencies verify submitted records, and what if checks fail?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: Non-citizens may draw a sixty-day photo-free temporary permit while agencies verify papers, denied if verification fails.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: Which five documents are accepted to prove and verify an applicant's Social Security number?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: Social Security numbers are collected and verified; cards, W-two forms, full-number paychecks, one thousand ninety-nine forms, or military IDs prove them.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: Who must present one secondary identification item instead of a Social Security proof, and what kinds of records qualify?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: Numberless citizens and immigrants, plus all non-immigrants, supply one secondary item spanning licenses, military and school records, birth transcripts, seasoned life policies, draft and voter cards, court papers, foreign IDs, and weapon permits.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: How many residential address proofs are required, and which everyday household, vehicle, or insurance records count?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: Two address proofs come from leases, voter, vehicle, or vessel records, statements, utility hookups, booklets, service or medical cards, or insurance papers.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: Which school, mail, or shelter records also prove address, and what must you add if you live in someone else's home?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: Transcripts, professional licenses, tax forms, exchange certificates, shelter letters, bank and government mail, and offender forms also prove address, and housed applicants add a host letter.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: Which document formats pass counter inspection, which copies get rejected, and how are name differences resolved?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: Originals and certified copies pass, photocopies and notarized copies fail, and name gaps need a linking court or family paper.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: Can an applicant blend primary identification documents across citizen, immigrant, Canadian, and non-immigrant lists?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: Citizens, immigrants, Canadians, and non-immigrants each follow a separate primary-identification track with no mixing.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: How does Florida handle pending document verification versus a failed primary and secondary check?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: A sixty-day photo-free permit bridges agency verification, while failed primary and secondary checks end in denial.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.front: How does the required count for secondary identification compare with the required count for residential address proof?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.expected_back: Secondary identification needs one listed item for the numberless, while address proof always needs two residence papers.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: What age and test requirements separate getting a Florida learner's license from earning a full driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: Learners must be fifteen, trained, and vision- and knowledge-tested; drivers must be sixteen, identified, and skills-tested too.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: What five milestones covering hold time, driving record, certified hours, consent, and school must a minor meet for a license?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: Drivers under eighteen must hold a learner license for twelve months or until turning eighteen, whichever comes first, go twelve months without moving-violation convictions except one withheld adjudication, log at least fifty driving hours including ten at night certified by a parent, guardian, or responsible adult twenty-one or older, submit parental consent, and maintain school attendance.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: Who must complete Florida's substance-abuse course before getting a first license, and which graduates skip it?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: The substance-abuse course binds every never-licensed applicant, except certified school driver-education graduates.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: How does parental consent work for unmarried minors, and what replaces it for married or emancipated teens?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: Unmarried minors need a signed parental application whose signer accepts responsibility and may rescind it to cancel; married and emancipated minors show certificates or court orders instead.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.front: What health disclosures and physician reports are required at licensing, and what optional medical mark is available?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.expected_back: Drivers must disclose impairing conditions, secure a doctor report for seizures or blackouts, and may mark insulin dependence.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: What penalties hit drivers who ignore a license restriction, and what conditions do letter codes regulate?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: Defying a restriction draws a citation and suspension; letter codes cover lenses, hand controls, mirrors, daylight, and work limits.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: Which vehicle adaptations, medical alerts, and route limits are governed by numbered restriction codes?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: Numbered codes order business-only routes, interlocks, alert bracelets, automatic gears, power steering, signals, grips, pedals, and hearing aids.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.front: How does the age-fifteen learner package expand when stepping up to full licensure at sixteen?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.expected_back: Learner entry opens at fifteen with training and two tests, and full licensure at sixteen adds identification plus the skills test.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.front: Who can certify a minor's fifty driving hours, and how do convictions, school attendance, and age eighteen affect the upgrade?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.expected_back: Licensure under eighteen combines twelve months with a learner license or reaching age eighteen first, twelve conviction-free months aside from one withheld-adjudication moving violation, fifty practice hours with ten at night certified by a parent, guardian, or responsible adult twenty-one or older, parental consent, and school attendance compliance.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.front: Which specific credential lets a first-time Florida license seeker bypass the standalone substance-abuse course?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.expected_back: The substance course binds every never-licensed seeker, yet certified school driver-education graduates skip it.

sec01-card-sec01-R13.front: What legal power does a consenting adult retain over a minor's license, and which minors apply without adult consent?
sec01-card-sec01-R13.expected_back: A consenting adult accepts driving responsibility and may rescind it to cancel, while married and emancipated minors bypass consent.

sec01-card-sec01-R14.front: What extra destinations are allowed on a business-purpose restriction compared with an employment-only restriction?
sec01-card-sec01-R14.expected_back: Employment-only travel covers job trips while business-only reach extends to school, worship, and medical needs.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.front: At what age do Florida ID cards begin, how long do they last, can you hold one alongside a license, and who gets one free?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.expected_back: ID cards start at age five, run four years for young holders and eight beyond, never coexist with a license, and go free to qualifying homeless and poverty-level applicants.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.front: How quickly and where must registered career offenders report for card issuance and later updates?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.expected_back: Career offenders register in person within two working days and repeat at every renewal and address or name change.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.front: Which male age bracket faces Selective Service registration at licensing, and what deadline binds sexual offenders and predators?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.expected_back: Males eighteen to twenty-six must meet draft registration, and sexual offenders and predators must register within forty-eight hours.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.front: How do the printed designations differ between sexual offender and sexual predator cards, and how fast must changes be reported?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.expected_back: Offender cards print the statute tag and predator cards the predator label, and both groups report renewals and forty-eight-hour changes.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.front: Which three optional designations or charitable contributions can applicants add during licensing?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.expected_back: Donor registration, free veteran marks with discharge papers, and voluntary trust-fund gifts attach at application.

sec01-card-sec01-R15.front: How do Florida ID expiration terms split by age, and why must you surrender an ID when getting licensed?
sec01-card-sec01-R15.expected_back: Identification cards run four years for the young and eight beyond, and no driver may hold a license and a card together.

sec01-card-sec01-R16.front: How does the reporting clock for career offenders differ from the clock for sexual offenders and predators?
sec01-card-sec01-R16.expected_back: Career offenders answer within two working days while sexual offenders and predators answer within forty-eight hours.

sec01-card-sec01-R17.front: How do offender and predator card markings differ, and can a post-office box serve as a registered home address?
sec01-card-sec01-R17.expected_back: Offender cards carry the statute tag while predator cards carry the predator label, and post boxes never count as home.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.front: Within how many days must you update your license after moving, and which legal records back a name change?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.expected_back: Address moves need a new license within thirty days via portal or office, and name changes ride on marriage, divorce, or court papers.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.front: Which federal or foreign agencies must update your new name first before Florida prints a renamed credential?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.expected_back: Social Security, immigration, and Canadian passport records must be corrected before Florida reissues a renamed card.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.front: How can you replace a missing Florida license, and what waives the replacement fee when your wallet is stolen?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.expected_back: Lost cards are replaced promptly in person or online, free for theft victims bearing a police report.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.front: Which issue-date cutoff requires bringing a full REAL ID document set again, and how must non-immigrants renew or replace?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.expected_back: Full document sets return for anyone unissued since January one, two thousand ten, and non-immigrants renew and replace only in person.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.front: How long does a Class E license stay valid, what two things happen at renewal, and what four problems block renewal?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.expected_back: A Class E driver license remains valid for six to eight years; renewal requires presenting your old license and passing a vision exam, and is denied if you are ineligible, left a traffic summons unanswered, hold a suspended, revoked, or canceled license, or fail to present required documentation.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.front: When may citizens and immigrants use online renewal, what blocks consecutive online use, and what penalty hits past your birthday?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.expected_back: Citizens and immigrants renew online for six or eight years unless remote-renewed before or disqualified, and late filings past the birthday deadline add fifteen dollars.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.front: What vision requirement applies to Florida drivers aged eighty and older at every renewal, and what does the state screening cost?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.expected_back: Drivers eighty and older pass vision screening at no charge in person or by practitioner form before renewing.

sec01-card-sec01-R18.front: Why is waiting longer than thirty days to update a Florida address risky for drivers?
sec01-card-sec01-R18.expected_back: Any address move forces a new license within thirty days, and a stale card risks missed mail plus a citation.

sec01-card-sec01-R19.front: Besides bringing your prior license and passing vision, which four legal or document issues will stop a Class E renewal?
sec01-card-sec01-R19.expected_back: Class E renewal covers six to eight years upon showing your prior license and passing a vision exam, while ineligibility, an unanswered traffic summons, a suspended, revoked, or canceled license, or missing required documents prevents renewal.

sec01-card-sec01-R20.front: How does replacing a stolen card with a police report contrast with replacing a card unissued since before twenty-ten?
sec01-card-sec01-R20.expected_back: Theft victims with a police report replace free, while the long-unissued must rebuild the full document set.

sec01-card-sec01-R21.front: Which groups qualify for Florida's online renewal portal, and which two conditions force an office visit or clearance first?
sec01-card-sec01-R21.expected_back: Online renewal serves qualified citizens and immigrants but shuts out the recently remote-renewed and the suspended.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.front: What are Florida's standard fees for first licenses, learner permits, renewals, replacements, ID cards, and late renewals?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.expected_back: First licenses, learner permits, and renewals cost forty-eight dollars; replacements and ID cards cost twenty-five dollars; late renewals add fifteen dollars.

sec01-card-sec01-F37.front: What are the six Florida reinstatement fees for fraud, substance offenses, revocation, suspension, general lapses, and bad checks?
sec01-card-sec01-F37.expected_back: Reinstatement costs one hundred eighty dollars for fraud, one hundred thirty dollars for substance offenses, seventy-five dollars after revocation, forty-five dollars after suspension, sixty dollars for most lapses, and fifty-five dollars for bad checks.

sec01-card-sec01-F38.front: How does curing a liability-insurance lapse compare with the three escalating PIP lapse fees within three years?
sec01-card-sec01-F38.expected_back: Insurance lapses cost fifteen dollars for liability and one hundred fifty dollars, two hundred fifty dollars, then five hundred dollars across PIP suspensions inside three years, DUI cases included.

sec01-card-sec01-F39.front: What do written retests, road retests, endorsements, and tax-collector visits cost, and which veterans pay zero credential fees?
sec01-card-sec01-F39.memory_hook: Ten written, twenty skills, veterans free
sec01-card-sec01-F39.expected_back: Knowledge retests cost ten dollars, skills retests twenty dollars, endorsements seven dollars, and collector service six dollars and twenty-five cents; fully disabled veterans pay no license or ID fees.

sec01-card-sec01-R22.front: How do the three everyday dollar amounts divide across issuance or renewal, ID or replacement, and late renewal?
sec01-card-sec01-R22.expected_back: Licenses and renewals cost forty-eight dollars, replacements and ID cards twenty-five dollars, and late renewals add fifteen dollars.

sec01-card-sec01-R23.front: How do the reinstatement charges compare across suspension, payment lapses, revocation, and license fraud?
sec01-card-sec01-R23.expected_back: Revocation cures at seventy-five dollars, suspension at forty-five dollars, and most payment lapses at sixty dollars against fraud at one hundred eighty dollars.

sec01-card-sec01-R24.front: Why is a Personal Injury Protection lapse far costlier to cure than a fifteen-dollar liability lapse?
sec01-card-sec01-R24.expected_back: Liability lapses cure at fifteen dollars while injury-protection tiers climb one hundred fifty dollars, two hundred fifty dollars, then five hundred dollars inside three years.

sec01-card-sec01-R25.front: How does the knowledge retake charge compare with the driving-skills retake charge, and who receives free credentials?
sec01-card-sec01-R25.expected_back: Knowledge retests cost ten dollars against twenty dollars for skills, and fully disabled veterans pay nothing for licenses or IDs.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: Which two insurance coverages must be in place before registering a Florida vehicle, and who gets paid under each?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: Registration needs injury and property coverage first, with injury benefits paying your own hurt regardless of fault and property benefits paying damage you cause others.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.front: How much of each mandatory insurance coverage must Florida vehicle owners carry continuously, from whom, and where does proof stay?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.expected_back: Owners prove coverage at registration, carry at least ten thousand dollars of each kind from a Florida-licensed carrier, keep it continuous, and keep proof in the car.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: When does the ninety-day presence rule require Florida coverage, what happens upon a lapse, and what must you turn in before canceling a policy?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: Cars present ninety days in the last three hundred sixty-five must stay insured, carriers report lapses to the state, failures suspend for up to three years, and plates go back before policies cancel.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: What happens if an officer stops you without insurance proof in the car, and what reinstatement fee range hits convicted lapses?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: Stopped drivers without proof must prove coverage in court or face suspension, and convicted lapses reinstate between one hundred fifty dollars and five hundred dollars.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: What escalated penalties, license restrictions, fake-card charges, and hearing rights apply once an insurance suspension passes thirty days?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: Suspensions past thirty days allow plate seizure and jail time up to a year with a one thousand dollars fine, bar temporary licenses, punish fake cards as misdemeanors, and grant hearings on request.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: How can crash-involved drivers prove financial responsibility, and what three-year coverage limits hit DUI convictions?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: Crash drivers prove financial responsibility by insurance or state certificate, and DUI convicts carry one hundred thousand dollars, three hundred thousand dollars, and fifty thousand dollars tiers for three years.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: What bodily-injury and property coverage limits apply after crashes, high point totals, habitual-offender status, or serious offenses?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: Point, crash, habitual-offender, and serious-offense cases carry ten thousand dollars, twenty thousand dollars, and ten thousand dollars tiers or thirty thousand dollars combined, with lapses suspending up to three years and at-fault damages prepaid.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: What is the exact difference between who gets paid by injury coverage versus property damage liability?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: Injury coverage pays your own hurt no matter the fault while property coverage pays damage you inflict on others.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.front: How does a motorcycle's narrow outline trick your depth perception at intersections?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.expected_back: A bike's small profile fools depth perception, so it often looks much farther off than it truly is.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.front: Why is tailgating a motorcycle far riskier than following a heavy passenger car closely?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.expected_back: Never tailgate a motorcycle, since it can halt faster than surrounding cars.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.front: Why might a motorcycle slow down sharply ahead of you without its red brake light ever coming on?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.expected_back: Riders frequently slow by downshifting or easing the throttle, which never lights the brake lamp.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.front: What happens if your car buzzes past a motorcyclist with only a couple of feet to spare?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.expected_back: Never squeeze past a rider with only feet to spare, because the wind blast can throw the bike down.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.front: How should you steer and control your speed while a motorcycle passes your vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.expected_back: When a motorcycle overtakes you, hold your lane position and never accelerate.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.front: How many seconds of following distance belong behind a motorcycle in dry weather — and which six surface or weather hazards demand even more?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.expected_back: Keep more than a four-second gap behind motorcycles, widening it for foul weather, gusts, wet or icy pavement, potholes, gravel, and rail crossings.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.front: What simple habit before every lane change ranks among the best ways to protect nearby motorcyclists?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.expected_back: Always flash turn signals before lane changes, among the most protective acts for nearby riders.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.front: Why can you never rely solely on blind-spot alerts or driver-assistance cameras to detect motorcycles?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.expected_back: Driver-assist systems may miss motorcycles entirely, so watch your surroundings and honor every tip above.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: At which two everyday conflict points must motorists look extra closely for approaching motorcycles?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: Drivers must stay alert for motorcycles and look closely before entering any intersection or switching lanes.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: Which three factors combine to make motorcycles much harder to judge or detect than cars?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.memory_hook: Deceptive distance, unlit slows, missed sensors
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: Bikes look farther than they are, slow without brake lights, and dodge driver-assist sensors, a triple invisibility trap.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.front: How do the baseline motorcycle following cushion and rough-surface adjustments work together?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.memory_hook: Past four seconds, wider on hazards
sec12-card-sec12-R03.expected_back: Following a bike means no tailgating plus a gap past four seconds, stretched wider for weather, gusts, slick or broken pavement, gravel, and rails.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.front: Which three rules govern overtaking a motorcyclist, being overtaken by one, and moving between lanes?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.expected_back: Pass riders only with full room since wind blast topples, hold your lane when they pass you, and signal every lane change.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: How old must you be to operate a motorcycle or moped on a Florida public road?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: Operating a motorcycle or moped on a public road requires age sixteen or older.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.front: What twelve-month requirement must a sixteen- or seventeen-year-old complete before earning a Florida Motorcycle Only license?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.expected_back: Riders under eighteen must carry a learner license for twelve months with zero moving-violation convictions before earning a Motorcycle Only license.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.front: What training and credential combination is required to legally ride a motorcycle in Florida?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.expected_back: Motorcycle operators must finish an approved safety course plus hold a license endorsement or a Motorcycle Only license.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.front: What driver license class covers riding a moped in Florida — and is a motorcycle endorsement required?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.expected_back: Moped operators need a Class E driver license, with no motorcycle endorsement demanded.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.front: Who must always wear a motorcycle helmet in Florida, and what two requirements let an older rider go without one?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.expected_back: Helmets stay mandatory for riders under twenty-one; riders twenty-one or older may skip one only while carrying medical insurance paying at least ten thousand dollars for injuries.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.front: Are Florida motorcycle and moped operators required to carry Personal Injury Protection coverage?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.expected_back: Motorcycle and moped operators need not carry Personal Injury Protection insurance.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.front: How often must motorcycles and mopeds renew registration tags, and which paths are strictly off-limits to them?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.expected_back: Bikes and mopeds need yearly registration with the right tag and must stay off bicycle and foot paths.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.front: How do the age-sixteen floor, the under-eighteen clean learner year, and the safety-course rule build Florida's motorcycle path?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.expected_back: Public-road riding starts at sixteen, under-eighteen riders serve twelve clean learner months first, and motorcycle operation adds an approved course plus endorsement or Motorcycle Only license.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.front: What separates Florida's licensing rule for a moped from the rule for a full motorcycle?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.expected_back: Mopeds ask only a Class E license with no endorsement, a lighter ticket than the motorcycle course-plus-endorsement path.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.front: How do age twenty-one, ten thousand dollars of medical coverage, PIP rules, and yearly tags fit together for riders?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.expected_back: Helmets bind every rider under twenty-one while riders twenty-one and up escape only with ten thousand dollars medical coverage, PIP stays optional, and machines need annual tags while shunning bike and foot paths.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.front: When bicyclists, skateboarders, or skaters roll through a crosswalk or driveway, what legal status do they hold?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.expected_back: Motorists must do everything possible to avoid striking walkers, and riders on bikes, skateboards, or skates count as pedestrians inside crosswalks and driveways.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.front: What must you do when a pedestrian is crossing a street or driveway at an intersection or marked crossing?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.expected_back: Halt and stay halted for pedestrians crossing any street or driveway at marked crossings and intersections.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.front: Before pulling into or out of an alley, private road, or driveway across a sidewalk, what must you do for people walking?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.expected_back: Stop for sidewalk pedestrians whenever entering or leaving alleys, driveways, and private roads.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.front: When stopping at a red traffic signal, how much of your car may rest over the crosswalk lines?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.expected_back: Never clog a crosswalk at a red light or let any part of your car hang over it.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.front: Why is it strictly illegal to pass another vehicle stopped at a crosswalk — even if you see nobody walking?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.expected_back: Never overtake a car stopped at a crosswalk for a walker; always assume someone may be crossing even when nobody shows.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.front: Before making a legal right turn on a red light, what stop and directional scan are mandatory?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.expected_back: Stop fully before every right on red and scan both directions for crosswalk pedestrians.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.front: Around which specific groups of pedestrians must drivers come to a complete stop, yield, and exercise extra caution?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.memory_hook: Full stop for canes, wheelchairs, kids
sec12-card-sec12-F23.expected_back: Stop completely, yield, and take extra care around blind pedestrians with white canes tipped red or service animals, mobility-impaired people with walkers, crutches, orthopedic canes, wheelchairs, or guide dogs, and children or confused or incapacitated walkers.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.front: Why must drivers treat cyclists, skaters, and skateboarders inside crosswalks or driveways with pedestrian care?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.expected_back: Inside crosswalks and driveways, bike, skateboard, and skate riders legally become pedestrians whom drivers must strain to miss.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.front: Which five driver rules protect pedestrians across intersections, driveways, red lights, and multi-lane crossings?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.expected_back: Drivers halt and hold for crosswalk walkers, stop for sidewalk users at every alley and driveway mouth, never block or overhang crossings, never pass a car stopped for a walker, and always stop before right on red.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.front: Which mobility aids, service animals, and vulnerable groups always command a complete stop and extra caution?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.expected_back: Full stops with yields and extra caution go to white canes with red tips, service and guide animals, walkers, crutches, orthopedic canes, wheelchairs, children, and confused or incapacitated walkers.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.front: May a pedestrian walk along the paved street lane when a sidewalk is provided alongside it?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.expected_back: Walkers must leave the roadway whenever a sidewalk exists.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.front: When a road has no sidewalk at all, which shoulder and direction must a pedestrian use?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.expected_back: Without a sidewalk, walk the left shoulder facing oncoming traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.front: Where should pedestrians cross streets, and do intersection crosswalks always have painted lines?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.expected_back: Cross at intersections or marked crosswalks, noting intersection crosswalks may be marked or unmarked.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.front: Who holds the right-of-way when a pedestrian crosses a street mid-block outside any crosswalk?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.expected_back: Outside a crosswalk, pedestrians yield the right-of-way to vehicles.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.front: Even inside a painted crosswalk, when must a pedestrian yield the right-of-way to vehicles?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.expected_back: Walkers yield to vehicles in the crosswalk whenever the signal glows red or reads DON’T WALK.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.front: Which curb scan, visibility gear, and distraction rules protect pedestrians day and night?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.expected_back: Stay out from between parked cars, pause at the curb to look left, right, then left again, wear bright reflective neon and carry a flashlight after dark, and skip texting and headphones.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.front: When a public transit bus signals to re-enter your traffic lane from a designated pullout bay, what must you do?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.expected_back: Yield to same-direction transit buses signaling their return to traffic from signed pullout bays.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.front: How do sidewalks, left shoulders, crosswalks, and red signals together define where walkers walk and yield?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.expected_back: Walkers take sidewalks when present, face traffic on the left shoulder without one, cross at intersections or crosswalks, and yield to cars outside crossings or under red and DON’T WALK signals.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.front: Which four personal safety habits keep pedestrians visible and alert around traffic?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.expected_back: Street smarts mean crossing at crosswalks never between parked cars, looking left-right-left from the curb, glowing neon with a night flashlight, and ditching texts and headphones.

sec12-card-sec12-R13.front: Who holds the right-of-way when a public transit bus signals out of a signed pullout bay into your lane?
sec12-card-sec12-R13.expected_back: Same-direction buses flashing back into traffic from signed pullouts own the right-of-way over drivers.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.front: May you ever pass a school bus while its red stop signal is flashing and extended?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.memory_hook: Passing flashing school buses breaks law
sec12-card-sec12-F31.expected_back: Passing a school bus flashing its stop signal breaks the law.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.front: On an undivided two-way street, who must stop for a school bus loading or unloading kids, and when may traffic move again?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.expected_back: On undivided two-way roads, traffic in both directions stops for a bus loading or unloading children and waits until the signal drops and every child clears the road.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.front: What exact physical separation lets oncoming traffic keep moving past a stopped school bus — and why don't painted turn lanes count?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.expected_back: Opposite-direction drivers skip the stop only past a raised barrier or unpaved median at least five feet wide, since painted lines never qualify, while same-direction drivers always stop until the signal drops.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.front: In what order do school crossing guards enter and leave a crosswalk, and where must your front bumper stop?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.memory_hook: Guard first in, stop at line
sec12-card-sec12-F34.expected_back: Honor school zones, signs, and crossing guards who enter first and leave last, and stop at the stop line rather than inside the crosswalk when children or guards occupy it.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.front: Which farm vehicles must display a rear slow-moving vehicle emblem, which highways are excluded, and when can they run at night?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.expected_back: Farm rigs built under twenty-five miles per hour must show the slow-vehicle emblem on the rear on public highways outside interstates and run daylight-only without proper night lamps and reflectors.

sec12-card-sec12-F36.front: How do school-bus stopping duties compare across two-lane roads, multi-lane paved-across roads, and divided highways?
sec12-card-sec12-F36.expected_back: Paved-across two-lane and multi-lane roads order both directions to stop, while divided highways order only traffic behind the bus to stop and let opposite traffic proceed cautiously.

sec12-card-sec12-R14.front: What two conditions must both finish before either direction resumes driving past a school bus on an undivided road?
sec12-card-sec12-R14.expected_back: Stop-signal buses freeze both directions on undivided roads until the signal falls and children clear, and passing one is flatly illegal.

sec12-card-sec12-R15.front: Why do painted lines never excuse opposite traffic from stopping for a school bus, and what always applies behind the bus?
sec12-card-sec12-R15.expected_back: Only a raised barrier or unpaved median five feet or wider frees opposite traffic, paint never counts, same-direction drivers always halt, and divided roads free only the far side with caution.

sec12-card-sec12-R16.front: How do the crossing guard's entry-and-exit sequence and the painted stop line protect children in school zones?
sec12-card-sec12-R16.expected_back: School guards step in first and out last, and drivers yield to a stop at the line outside the crosswalk while children or guards hold it.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.question_text: What course must anyone who has never held a driver license complete before applying, and what can substitute?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.teaching_text: Completing an approved school-board driver class lets first-timers skip taking the standalone drug-and-alcohol course.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.question_text: Which blood-alcohol range triggers mandatory substance-course completion before an under-twenty-one driver can regain hardship driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.teaching_text: Zero-tolerance suspensions block young drivers even from hardship commuting until that substance class finishes.
sec02-card-sec02-F02.must_match_memory_hook: Point zero two to five, course

visual_sync.text_span: Point zero two to five, course

sec02-card-sec02-R01.question_text: Which two distinct groups of Florida drivers are gated by the substance-abuse course?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.teaching_text: One curriculum serves both brand-new license seekers and under-twenty-one drivers clearing zero-tolerance suspensions.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.question_text: Which crash patterns and four moving convictions make Basic Driver Improvement school mandatory?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.teaching_text: Passing a stopped school bus or blowing a red light triggers state-ordered retraining automatically.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.question_text: Who qualifies to elect driver improvement school on a ticket, what speed disqualifies you, and how much civil penalty drops?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.teaching_text: Commercial rig operators and speeders clocked past thirty over lose the point-avoidance school option.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.question_text: How does mandatory driver improvement school differ in trigger and purpose from elective traffic school?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.teaching_text: State-mandated classes remediate dangerous wrecks or convictions, whereas voluntary elections shield clean driving records.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.question_text: What three ticket conditions keep traffic-school election open, and what percentage discount does it earn?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.teaching_text: Checking your citation speed and vehicle class confirms eligibility before notifying the county clerk.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.question_text: How does electing school shield your auto insurance, and which three situations strip that protection away?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.teaching_text: Even when points stay off past fifteen over, insurers can still raise premiums above that mark.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.question_text: How far apart must traffic-school elections sit, what is the lifetime limit, and what is your county-clerk deadline?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.teaching_text: Missing the thirty-day clerk notification window forfeits withheld adjudication and puts points on record.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.question_text: Which license suspensions and out-of-state ticket situations are handled by Advanced Driver Improvement courses?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.teaching_text: Once accumulated points or habitual status suspend driving, basic ticket school no longer suffices.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.question_text: What offenses require licensed DUI programs, and what benefits do refresher courses offer drivers past sixty-five?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.teaching_text: Refusing a lawful breath or blood test triggers DUI program enrollment even without a conviction.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.question_text: Which three specific thresholds break the auto-insurance rate shelter normally earned by electing school?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.teaching_text: Notice how fifteen over breaks insurance shelter while thirty over blocks electing school altogether.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.question_text: What three numbers govern election spacing, lifetime total, and clerk notification for Florida traffic school?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.teaching_text: Burning all five lifetime elections early leaves zero point-avoidance cushion for decades of driving.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.question_text: How do Florida's specialty education tracks divide across suspended drivers, impairment cases, and drivers over sixty-five?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.teaching_text: Enrolling in the wrong course type wastes tuition because courts and insurers demand exact matches.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.question_text: Which four core abilities do Florida driver-license examinations verify first?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.teaching_text: Testing reading, rules, eyesight, and road handling together ensures every new motorist shares streets safely.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.question_text: What fifth safety screening purpose do license exams serve, and which three venues administer Florida testing?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.teaching_text: Checking physical and mental readiness alongside flexible school and third-party testing keeps access safe.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.question_text: Who can take the knowledge exam online, how do third-party testers operate, and what catch applies to school-program passes?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.teaching_text: Adults eighteen and older test in person, and random counter retests keep outside providers honest.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.question_text: Which three exam stages apply to original applicants, and how does Florida treat corrective lenses versus telescopic lenses?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.teaching_text: Telescopic magnification narrows side awareness dangerously, so applicants cannot use telescopic lenses to pass.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.question_text: What are Florida's exact acuity cutoffs for passing, specialist referral, twenty-over-seventy eligibility, one-eye vision, and field width?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.teaching_text: If one eye sees two hundred or worse, the stronger eye must hit twenty-forty.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.question_text: How do Florida's three in-person testing venues pair with the minor-only online option?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.teaching_text: Even minors who finish the written exam at home still appear in person for vision.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.question_text: How do twenty-over-forty, twenty-over-fifty, twenty-over-seventy, and one hundred thirty degrees fit together on the eye check?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.teaching_text: Knowing each acuity step plus the hundred-thirty-degree horizontal span nails tricky Florida vision questions.
sec02-card-sec02-R08.must_match_memory_hook: Forty clears, fifty refers, seventy conditions

visual_sync.text_span: Forty clears, fifty refers, seventy conditions

sec02-card-sec02-F14.question_text: How many multiple-choice questions appear on Florida's Class E knowledge exam, and what three topics do they test?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.teaching_text: Expect road-sign and lane-marking identification woven directly alongside statutory traffic rules and defensive habits.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.question_text: Which three subject areas fill the fifty items on the Florida knowledge test?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.teaching_text: Skipping sign shapes or safe-following habits leaves gaps across a third of your fifty questions.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.question_text: Who provides the car for the driving-skills exam, and which defects or vehicle builds trigger an automatic pre-drive rejection?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.teaching_text: Examiners walk around your car first and cancel road tests over inoperable doors, signals, or tags.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.question_text: What paperwork and seven equipment areas must pass inspection before an examiner steps into your test vehicle?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.teaching_text: Checking brake lights, turn lamps, horn, and passenger door latches beforehand saves forfeiting your appointment.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.question_text: How far must you back straight without using mirrors on the skills test, and what following gap and intersection habits are graded?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.teaching_text: Staring into your rearview mirror or backup camera instead of looking back loses backing points.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.question_text: What four skills covering right-of-way, hills, overtaking, and turn-signal distance appear next on the road exam?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.teaching_text: Examiners ask how you would park on an imaginary hill even on flat Florida lots.

sec02-card-sec02-R11.question_text: Which three exact numbers govern straight backing, following cushion, and turn signaling during the Florida skills test?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.teaching_text: Locking down fifty feet, three to four seconds, and one hundred feet hits every metric.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.question_text: Which five driving tasks close out the Florida skills test, including the width of the three-point-turn zone, and what follows?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.teaching_text: Stopping smoothly at twenty miles per hour without skidding and centering between lines seals passing.

sec02-card-sec02-R12.question_text: Within what roadway width must you complete the three-point turn while maintaining proper driving posture?
sec02-card-sec02-R12.teaching_text: Touching curbs or slouching one-handed during your tight turnabout costs avoidable road-test deductions.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: Which four exterior items and tinted-glass mirror rule come first before driving, and what six cabin checks follow?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Darkened rear windows block center-mirror clarity, triggering Florida's requirement for two outside mirrors reaching two hundred feet behind.
sec07-card-sec07-F01.must_match_memory_hook: Exterior gear first, cabin setup next

visual_sync.text_span: Exterior gear first, cabin setup next

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: What check comes before getting in to reverse, how should your body face while backing, and can cameras replace looking?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Toddlers and pets vanish below trunk height on screens and mirrors, making a walk-around and direct rear-window turn essential.
sec07-card-sec07-F02.must_match_memory_hook: Walk behind, look through rear glass

visual_sync.text_span: Walk behind, look through rear glass

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: Where do blind zones sit around your car, how do you clear them before moving over, and how do truck blind zones compare?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Lingering beside a semi-trailer's rear corners hides your entire car from the trucker's mirrors.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: Walk through the two-stage Florida pre-drive order from outside hardware and rear-tint mirrors to inside cabin readiness?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: Adjusting your seat and mirrors while still in Park stops awkward reaching once the car rolls into traffic.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: While reversing, how should you position your arm and eyes, how fast should you roll, and how do spotters or cameras fit in?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Reversing at a walking crawl gives you instant stopping margin if someone steps into your path.
sec07-card-sec07-R02.must_match_memory_hook: Turn over seat, creep with spotters

visual_sync.text_span: Turn over seat, creep with spotters

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: Why are mirrors alone never enough for rear-flank blind corners, and how does vehicle size change blind-zone risk?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: Quick shoulder glances catch motorcycles tucked beside your quarter panels, and commercial trucks carry massive no-zones.
sec07-card-sec07-R03.must_match_memory_hook: Glance past mirrors, respect big rigs

visual_sync.text_span: Glance past mirrors, respect big rigs

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: How long do alert perception and reaction each take, and how far do you roll at fifty miles per hour during reaction alone?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Your car covers nearly four car lengths at fifty miles per hour before your foot even touches the brake pedal.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: At fifty miles per hour on dry pavement, what are braking distance and total stopping distance, and how does multiplying speed multiply braking?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Doubling speed quadruples braking distance and tripling speed multiplies it ninefold because kinetic energy scales by the square.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: What minimum following cushion does Florida recommend, how do you time it, and which five conditions call for extra seconds?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Count four full seconds after the rear bumper ahead passes a fixed shadow or post before your front bumper reaches it.
sec07-card-sec07-F06.must_match_memory_hook: Four seconds minimum, stretch in hazards

visual_sync.text_span: Four seconds minimum, stretch in hazards

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: Which four vehicle types need extra following room, how far back must you trail a responding fire truck, and how do you handle tailgaters?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: Brake-checking a tailgater invites a high-speed rear-end crash; ease off the gas in the right lane so they pass.
sec07-card-sec07-F07.must_match_memory_hook: Five hundred firetrucks, ease right tailgaters

visual_sync.text_span: Five hundred firetrucks, ease right tailgaters

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: Pair the time range for perception and reaction with the reaction distance traveled at fifty miles per hour?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Fatigue, phones, or alcohol stretch both human split-seconds far beyond the alert fifty-five-foot baseline.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: Contrast pure braking feet with total stopping feet at fifty miles per hour, and state what doubling speed does?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: Adding perception and reaction onto one hundred fifty-eight braking feet pushes total dry-road stopping to two hundred sixty-eight.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: How do you measure Florida's four-second following rule, and which five situations demand stretching it wider?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Heavy cargo, wet asphalt, night glare, passing setups, and uphill climbs all eat into your stopping margin.
sec07-card-sec07-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Count four past markers, widen early

visual_sync.text_span: Count four past markers, widen early

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: How far apart must heavy trucks or tows stay outside cities, and what five right-of-way rules clear intersections?

sec07-card-sec07-R24.question_text: Which two vehicle categories may enter diamond-marked HOV lanes at designated openings?

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: Why must you never jerk the wheel into oncoming traffic or off the shoulder to dodge an animal in Florida?

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: Which daily light windows, roadside terrains, visual cues, and autumn months demand peak animal watchfulness in Florida?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Scanning ditch edges at twilight catches glowing animal eyes before deer bolt across rural woodland corridors.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: How should you warn other drivers, use your brakes and horn, and check mirrors when an animal stands near your lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Slamming the brakes with a tailgater glued to your bumper trades a deer scare for an instant rear-end wreck.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: How should you steer during an unavoidable animal impact, and who must you contact after hitting a large animal?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Large animals left in dark travel lanes trigger secondary pileups unless officers respond to clear the roadway.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: How does Florida pair its ban on swerving for wildlife with your duty after striking a large animal?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Exam questions pair those two rules so drivers neither yank the wheel in panic nor drive off silently afterward.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: Which four timing, sign, sight, and seasonal factors tell you where wildlife strikes spike?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Where one deer bounds out of timber near water in November, two or three followers usually trail right behind.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: How do headlight flashes affect other drivers versus deer, and what condition allows hard braking?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: Staring straight into bright beams locks deer in place on the centerline until horn blasts break the trance.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: Which headlight setting, glass tools, and pavement guides should you use in thick Florida smoke, fog, or heavy rain?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: High beams bounce straight off fog droplets and wildfire smoke into your eyes, blinding you behind a white wall.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: Beyond turning on low beams, what cabin, traffic-scanning, and vehicle-prep habits keep you safe in low visibility?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Drivers ahead sometimes panic-stop on the travel lane in heavy smoke, turning unlit tail ends into sudden traps.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: What lighting law fires whenever your wipers run in rain, and why do the first minutes of a shower stretch stopping distance?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: Fresh raindrops lift weeks of dripped engine grease into a soapy film before heavier downpours wash the asphalt clean.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: What happens to your tires during hydroplaning, and which three tire or speed factors trigger it sooner?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Once water wedges beneath spinning rubber, steering and braking vanish completely until speed drops back down.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: How do soaked brakes misbehave until dried, and what rule governs driving into a flooded Florida roadway?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: Standing storm water hides washed-out culverts and swift currents capable of sweeping passenger cars off the pavement.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: Why are parking lamps illegal as a substitute in fog or smoke, and what combination must you run instead?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Classic Florida exam trap: parking lights never satisfy low-visibility headlight laws during smoke, fog, or rain.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: Which three focus, scanning, and maintenance habits pair up during murky weather?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: Grimy windshields scatter oncoming glare across hazy glass while radio noise steals reaction time from creeping traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: How do Florida's wiper-headlight rule, oily early showers, and following-distance adjustments connect?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Doubling your dry-pavement cushion gives tires space to bite through slick road grime without rear-ending traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.question_text: Which three tire-condition and speed mistakes make floating tires skid hardest on wet pavement?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.teaching_text: Checking tire inflation and tread depth monthly keeps deep channels open to pump storm water out from under your wheels.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.question_text: How do you recover brakes splashed through a shallow puddle versus handling a flooded street ahead?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.teaching_text: Lightly riding the brake pedal warms wet rotors dry after unavoidable puddles, whereas deep water across lanes means turning back.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: How many feet ahead do high beams illuminate, above what speed do they help on open roads, and how does glare affect night vision?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Memorize four hundred fifty feet for Florida high-beam reach so you pace dark-road speed inside what your lamps actually show.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: When must headlights run at night, at what exact distances must high beams dim, and what rules cover parking lights?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Exam questions love swapping five hundred feet for oncoming cars with three hundred feet when trailing behind someone.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: How do you avoid overdriving headlights, protect night vision from bright glare, and pass an oncoming vehicle showing just one headlight?

sec08-card-sec08-R09.question_text: Compare the required dimming distance for approaching versus followed traffic, and can you drive dusk-to-dawn on parking lamps?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.teaching_text: Blasting high beams inside three hundred feet turns the lead driver's rearview mirror into a blinding spotlight.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.question_text: Which four visual and lane-positioning habits protect you from dark stops, bright glare, and one-headlight traffic?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.teaching_text: Looking briefly toward the white right-edge stripe spares your pupils from oncoming high beams while keeping lane position true.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: How does Florida licensing distinguish between immigrants, non-immigrants, and United States citizens?

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: How soon must working or schooling newcomers get a Florida license, and which four groups are excused?

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: Which three student, worker, and equipment-operator groups are also exempt from needing a Florida license?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Campus enrollees and home-licensed farm crews keep out-of-state driving privileges without switching cards.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: How do the triggers for general Florida residency differ from the specific thirty-day license deadline?

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: Which three weight, passenger, or cargo thresholds require upgrading to a commercial driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: Even a lightweight van triggers commercial rules once it carries sixteen occupants or placarded hazardous cargo.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: Which four document categories make up a Florida license application packet, and how must name changes be connected?

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: Which official documents qualify as primary identification for a United States citizen?

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: What primary identification records do lawful immigrants present, and how are Canadians and non-immigrants handled?
